text:
sam: just finished the first pass bring-up for the new multilingual embed model (m-embed-v2-int8). quick summary below, posting raw numbers + a couple plots in #eng-ml-artifacts
anya: awesome — did you run the cross-lang recall set we discussed? en->es, en->fr, en->zh?
sam: yes. used the 10k crosslang holdout (balanced by language). recall@1/5/10:
- en->en: 0.78 / 0.89 / 0.93
- en->es: 0.62 / 0.78 / 0.84
- en->fr: 0.60 / 0.76 / 0.82
- en->zh: 0.47 / 0.66 / 0.74
corey: hmm en->zh looks notably lower than expected. what's baseline for fp16 m-embed-v1?
sam: baseline fp16 (v1): en->zh: 0.55 / 0.71 / 0.78. so int8 dropped about 8-10% absolute at R@1.
dana: could be quantization bias for CJK tokenization or KV cache differences. did you try symmetric vs dynamic quant flags?
sam: tried default dynamic quant; symmetric produced similar R@1 but slightly worse R@10. attached eval args: ```python eval.py --model m-embed-v2 --quant int8 --quant-mode dynamic --holdout crosslang_10k --metrics recall@1,5,10,ndcg``` 
anya: can you push the per-language embedding distance histograms? want to check margin separation and if en-zh nearest neighbors are contaminated by script-level artifacts.
sam: posted histograms and a UMAP projection (color by language) in eng-ml-artifacts. quick observation: zh cluster is tighter but slightly shifted from en cluster; nearest neighbor distances for zh are lower overall (smaller intra-cluster distances) but cross-language margin is smaller.
corey: this suggests calibration issue — maybe apply per-lang centering / mean-shift before similarity? also try cosine vs dot product; any change?
sam: cosine vs dot: cosine improves en->zh R@1 by +0.02 (from 0.47 to 0.49). not enough. tried per-lang centering (subtract language mean computed on train) — en->zh R@1 up to 0.51.
dana: good signal. still not matching fp16 baseline though. did you run a small retrain/onboard step (sparse fine-tune on multilingual anchors)? or just pure quantization at export?
sam: just post-export quantization in this pass. plan is to run a tiny calibration fine-tune on anchor pairs next week if team agrees.
anya: for rollout gating we should set per-lang R@1 thresholds relative to baseline, e.g., allow -3% for en/fr/es but require -1% for zh. otherwise product hits for zh are risky.
corey: agree. also add a quality check: nearest-neighbor language match rate (should be >0.9 for same-lang retrieval). what are those numbers?
sam: same-lang match rates (top1): en 0.94, es 0.89, fr 0.88, zh 0.81.
dana: zh is the outlier. propose steps:
1) run symmetric quant + per-layer calibration tables (one more quant pass) — script: `scripts/quant_calibrate.sh m-embed-v2 --langs zh,en,es,fr`
2) run small 1k-anchor fine-tune with multilingual mining (LR 2e-5, 1 epoch)
3) re-eval recall & NN language match
4) if still low, consider model variant (m-embed-v2-large) or keep fp16 for zh-heavy customers.
sam: I'll kick off step1 now and post logs. ETA ~2h.
eval-bot: run started for job 1832110100 (quant_calibrate, model=m-embed-v2, modes=[sym,per-layer], langs=[zh,en,es,fr]) — will post summary when finished.
anya: also add a quick clustering stability check (kmeans over 50 seeds) and report silhouette per-lang. can help detect brittleness.
corey: and add a small human eval sample for zh — 200 pairs to sanity-check semantic equivalence. automatic metrics can miss translation idiosyncrasies.
sam: noted. will add both. will update thread with numbers and whether we should hold rollout for int8 or gate by region.
anya: thanks — really helpful. :thumbsup:
sam: np, will report back later with the bot output and next results.
